    "263092260c1ac0fda724743b2669b31affb56d4e": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-23T09:55:46Z",
      "body": "The third D-52 condition — every reader on one access point — was shown in\ne02c915. This commit takes the copy away:\n\n- .beads/issues.jsonl is no longer tracked, and is git-ignored so a\n  `git add -A` cannot bring it back. The export-identity gate and its four\n  tests are retired: there is no committed file left to compare.\n- The hosted CI hydrates the tracker, renders once and presets BEAD_RENDER;\n  every gate of the run reads that one render. Locally the access point\n  (scripts/bead_render.py) renders fresh through tools/bd, and without bd it\n  fails with both ways out — bootstrap or BEAD_RENDER — instead of reading a\n  stale copy.\n- The drift job hydrates too: plans-registry-strict reads the tracker, and\n  without the copy it would have crashed nightly. plans-registry and\n  plans-registry-strict declare needs_tracker; the schema now allows it in\n  both jobs.\n- The kit role geruest is dissolved: without the copy its remaining members\n  map to one export verdict, which the AK-6 test forbids. The stub files stay\n  with the export manifest. Two REIST_NICHT entries for tests that do not\n  travel were removed; the probe cap stays at 31.\n- verify_all.sh --ci measures the same gate set as the derived workflow\n  (finding 2 of the PR #32 review).\n- AGENTS.md house rules 2 and 4, README, plans/_README.md: the render is the\n  contract; a pull request body names every bead it opens, changes or closes\n  (maintainer, 2026-09-23, D-52 successor; the CI job summary follows as\n  bead coding-harness-1jg.4).\n- The empty gate-placement change package is archived (its bead 1jg.2 closed\n  with PR #32).\n\nStarted by a Cline session that stopped mid-way (uncommitted, last edit\n10:28); finished and corrected by Claude Code.\n\nVerified 2026-09-23: make verify VERIFY GREEN (325 passed, 15 skipped);\nverify_all.sh --job drift VERIFY GREEN, measuring the tracker locally.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T12:36:01Z",
      "body": "The maintainer decided on 2026-09-30 how Coding Harness tells an answer\nthe maintainer gave from one an agent wrote, without commit signing: a\ndecision takes effect only when the pull request that carries it is\nmerged by the maintainer or on their explicit request. The spec's open\ndecision is now answered, and the spec follows from it:\n\n- The gate stays an offline existence and format check; it cannot see who\n  merged, and the spec says so.\n- The command gains a way to record an answer the maintainer stated in the\n  conversation (--change, --answer, --reason, --stated-in), since the\n  maintainer often answers from a phone. The terminal path stays.\n- Merges through gh pr merge, the gh api merge calls and a GitHub MCP\n  merge tool ask first (permissions.ask). An agent never merges on its own\n  initiative, only on the maintainer's request, after restating the\n  decision block. A rule, not proof: agents act under the maintainer's\n  GitHub account. A separate bot identity is on the not-now list.\n- A pull request that carries a decision is marked: a label and a decision\n  block at the top of its body. The wording comes from a research note.\n\nresearch.md records what Claude Code documents about ask rules and the one\ntest that pins the ask list today.\n\nBead coding-harness-3ar: spec revised; the tracker was not written.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",

    "665de6828e272626498d040f625c064612023c02": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T12:29:38Z",
      "body": "The ADR answer gets its home in Coding Harness. Every change spec states\none of four classes in its header; a feature carries the ADR question as\na proposal; the maintainer's answer lives in\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the pilot's format (schema_version\n1), so LakeSwitch can later switch without migrating anything. A gate holds\nevery feature, active or archived, to its answer, and the command\n`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr` puts the open questions.\n\nThe maintainer directed on 2026-09-30 that Coding Harness introduces no\ncommit signing. How an answer is confirmed as the maintainer's, in a way\nno agent can perform on their behalf, is therefore an open decision in\nthe spec, with the requirement stated and the mechanism kept replaceable.\nPhase 3 waits for it.\n\nresearch.md gains its corrections after verification against the pilot\nand the gaps closed in this phase. plans/INDEX.md is regenerated.\n\nBead coding-harness-3ar: spec written; the tracker was not written.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-11-20T11:20:58Z",
      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7) is carried into\nmain's structure; nothing of either side is reverted.\n\nConflict resolutions:\n\n- scripts/verify_duration.py: main's in-process writers stay (record_start,\n  record_gate, record_end with root, state_root and env). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",

      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "decisions/gates.yaml",
        "provenance.yaml",
        "scripts/harness.py",
        "tests/test_harness_decide_adr.py"
      ]
    },
    "9446abe50f3a259d0ff515c3123ea5197f0f9293": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-20T23:42:48Z",
      "body": "decisions/gates.yaml declares what each gate measures, and thereby what reaches a\nmerge.       "body": "check_frontmatter_current.py holds every Markdown file whose provenance\nprefix declares `frontmatter: required` to one rule: its `updated:` date is\nnot older than the file's last change. The reference date of a clean file is\nthe committer date of the newest non-merge commit that changed it; of an\nuntracked or modified file, today. A shallow clone is refused (exit 3), not\nguessed at. `--stamp` sets `updated:` by editing that one line.\n\nThe tests build their own repositories; each rule sits next to the fault\nthat turns it red (sixteen planted faults, all red).\n\nBead coding-harness-qd7. Not yet wired into the gate list; that follows.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HRfJHTtj6rvcgudkYjJoP7\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "ea2d6283b189ae3ef790f8c5f765c018276dfd4e",
      "subject": "feat(scripts): add the check and the stamp for current document headers",

      ]
    },

      "body": "The orchestrator applies the held-path step of the plan, as the maintainer\ndecided on 2026-11-20:\n\n- model-endpoints.yaml declares the `spec_review` block the runner reads:\n  call limit 30 minutes, pause 30 seconds, fallback deepseek-v4.1-flash on\n  opencode-go (L3-2).\n- AGENTS.md and docs/WORKFLOW.md no longer call phase 2a optional; the class\n  table requires the review for bounded, feature and architectural changes;\n  the class paragraph says implement checks the class on every route; the\n  draft chain repeats draft and review up to round three, with the final\n  draft and the recorded fourth-round form; a new subsection states what\n  counts, currency, retry and fallback, the re-check and the inventory\n  (L2-8, L2-11, L3-3, L3-4). README's phase line follows.\n- prompts/02-spec.md and prompts/02a-spec-review.md state the re-review, the\n  strict severities and the exact `No finding.` answer (L3-6).\n- The handover skill runs `--spec-review-inventory` in the morning handover\n  (L3-10).\n- The criterion 1-3 tests read every workflow text and went red against the\n  old texts by hand; new tests anchor the prompt format, the repository's\n  declaration and the skill (L2-12, L3-5). The test world drops the real\n  `spec_review` block so fixtures declare their own.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_admission(root: Path, change: str) -> ReviewAdmission:\n    \"\"\"Why the change may not start a model yet, or the admission that lets it (spec criteria 4-9, 18-19).\n\n    One check for every implement route and for the morning inventory: the class must be\n    stated and agreeing, a spike stands outside the review rule, and a bounded, feature or\n    architectural change needs a qualifying, current spec review with no open ambiguity -\n    after three rounds a changed spec body is admitted on the review it has, an open\n    ambiguity never is. A previously implemented change faces the same check again. A change\n    whose class is refused is measured for its review as well, so the inventory lists it in\n    every group whose check it fails; implement names the class first.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        klass = declared_class(root, change, None)\n    except Refused as error:\n        part = _review_part(root, change, None)\n        return ReviewAdmission(\n            class_problem=str(error),\n            review_problem=part.review_problem,\n            left_out=part.left_out,\n            rounds=part.rounds,\n            recheck=part.recheck,\n        )\n    if klass == \"spike\":\n        return ReviewAdmission(klass=klass)\n    return _review_part(root, change, klass)\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::### Artefact lifecycle",
          "end_line": 423,
          "excerpt": "### Artefact lifecycle\n\n```\nplans/specs/<capability>/spec.md          LIVING      — what should hold today\nplans/changes/<name>/                     ACTIVE      — one change in flight\nplans/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/  HISTORICAL  — closed\ndocs/adr/NNNN-title.md                    PERMANENT   — append-only\n```\n\nTwo separate status fields: `status` moves when the project decides;\n`implementation_status` when the code moves. One field for both cannot say\nwhether an accepted spec is still unbuilt or whether built code rests on a\nwithdrawn spec — and those are exactly the interesting cases.\n\nOn close: the delta into the living capability spec, permanent architectural\ndecisions as an ADR, the rest into the archive. **An implemented feature spec\ndoes not stay as a living document** — the code and the git history are the\ntruth. Details in [`plans/_README.md`](../plans/_README.md).\n\nThe **rule against making a second one** stands verbatim in `AGENTS.md`, because\nan agent does not necessarily read `plans/_README.md`: before an artefact is\ncreated, search with `rg` first; where one exists, it is updated. `make\nstaleness` checks the consequences — missing frontmatter, contradictory status,\ndone and never archived, one-sided supersession.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/WORKFLOW.md",
          "reference": "### Artefact lifecycle",
          "start_line": 399,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }

          "end_line": 13267,
          "excerpt": "def review_loop(root: Path, change: str, availability_reported: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One round of phase 4b, until a round is clean (ADR 0021).\n\n    A fresh run discovers its free members through a forced live refresh and\n    pins the stage snapshot; every later call takes the run's next unconsumed\n    stage. The stops come before any stage: undecided or evidence-incomplete\n    rows first, then a clean previous round, then the repair brake (two\n    consecutive rounds whose accepted findings all begin `fix-r`), then spent\n    stages - each naming the round or the maintainer, and none reset by a\n    release or an edited configuration (ADR 0021, decision 9). One call\n    completes one round; a swarm's members run concurrently and merge into one\n    heading and one id series; an attempt whose every member failed completes\n    no round and consumes no stage.\n    \"\"\"\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = undecided_refusal(record_rows(record), \"decide them first\")\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    findings_text = \"\"\n    findings_path = folder_of(root, change) / \"findings.md\"\n    if findings_path.exists():\n        findings_text = findings_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, findings_text)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = released_overlap_refusal(record, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is None:\n        refusal = lost_record_refusal(change, root, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    # The snapshot before the stops: a released block without the runner's snapshot is refused here,\n    # never read as a finished run (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n    state = None if restarted_fresh(record, findings_text) else read_state(record, findings_text)\n    # After a maintainer's restart the stops read only the rounds that followed it (restart amendment).\n    floor = restart_floor(findings_text)\n    history = {number: rows for number, rows in history_rounds(record, findings_text).items() if number > floor}\n    # A round that found nothing has a heading but no row: it is counted by its heading.\n    last = max(max(history, default=0), rounds_run(record, findings_text))\n    if last > floor:\n        refusal = undecided_refusal(history.get(last, []), \"decide them first\")\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n        if clean_round(history.get(last, []), last) and not round_was_cut(record, last, findings_text):\n            raise CleanStop(f\"round {last} was clean: every row was decided and none accepted; the loop stops.\")\n        if (\n            last in history\n            and last - 1 in history\n            and fix_r_only(history[last], last)\n            and fix_r_only(history[last - 1], last - 1)\n        ):\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"rounds {last - 1} and {last} accepted only findings whose Origin begins `fix-r`; \"\n                \"the repair brake stops the loop; the maintainer decides what continues.\"\n            )\n    # Warn before admission and leak checks can refuse a call, including saved runs.\n    for warning in retain_terms_warnings(terms_warnings(endpoint_entry(root))):\n        print(f\"review-loop: Notice: {warning}.\", file=sys.stderr)\n    receipt_taken = False\n    if record is None and state is None:\n        # A fresh run has neither a record nor a released snapshot. read_state\n        # refuses a pre-swarm record without its Loop state line.\n        problem = entry_problem(root, OPENCODE)\n        if problem:\n            raise Refused(problem)\n        imp",

          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, ask: Ask = input, out: Out = print, today: date | None = None) -> int:\n    args = parser().parse_args(argv)\n    root: Path = args.root.resolve()\n    try:\n        if args.verb == \"time-log\":\n            return time_log(root, args, out=out, today=today or date.today())\n        given: dict[str, Any] = {name: getattr(args, name) for name in RECORDING}\n        if any(v is not None for v in given.values()):\n            flags = {name: \"--\" + name.replace(\"_\", \"-\") for name in RECORDING}\n            absent = [flags[n] for n, v in given.items() if v is None or not str(v).strip()]\n            if absent:\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"recording an answer needs all four of {', '.join(flags.values())}; missing or blank: {', '.join(absent)}\"\n                )\n        role = answering_role(root)\n        message = message_path(root)\n        day = today or date.today()\n        if given[\"change\"] is not None:\n            return record_adr(\n                root,\n                given[\"change\"],\n                given[\"answer\"],\n                given[\"reason\"],\n                given[\"stated_in\"],\n                out=out,\n                today=day,\n                role=role,\n                message_path=message,\n            )\n        if not sys.stdin.isatty():\n            raise Refused(\n                \"run this yourself in a terminal — the questions are for the maintainer to answer; \"\n                \"an answer stated elsewhere is recorded with --change, --answer, --reason and --stated-in\"\n            )\n        return decide_adr(root, ask=ask, out=out, today=day",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1506,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.       "statement": "The runner CLI is a single argparse surface in `main` (positional verb, change, ROW=STATUS, REASON, plus per-verb flags --stage2-off, --model, --class, --availability-reported, --seats, --handover, --stage-failed, --reason, --restart, --spec-review-inventory, --supersedes, --root). `_run` re-validates each flag against the verb (e.g. --stage2-off only for explore/implement/repair; --class only for explore/prepare-explore), rebuilds the known-verb list as `sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"])`, and maps Refused to exit 2, CallFailed to exit 1 and CleanStop to a clean-loop code — so adding a verb touches at least three code sites: the dict, the known list, and the dispatch chain in `_run`/`main`."

          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, ask: Ask = input, out: Out = print, today: date | None = None) -> int:\n    args = parser().parse_args(argv)\n    root: Path = args.root.resolve()\n    try:\n        if args.verb == \"time-log\":\n            return time_log(root, args, out=out, today=today or date.today())\n        given: dict[str, Any] = {name: getattr(args, name) for name in RECORDING}\n        if any(v is not None for v in given.values()):\n            flags = {name: \"--\" + name.replace(\"_\", \"-\") for name in RECORDING}\n            absent = [flags[n] for n, v in given.items() if v is None or not str(v).strip()]\n            if absent:\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"recording an answer needs all four of {', '.join(flags.values())}; missing or blank: {', '.join(absent)}\"\n                )\n        role = answering_role(root)\n        message = message_path(root)\n        day = today or date.today()\n        if given[\"change\"] is not None:\n            return record_adr(\n                root,\n                given[\"change\"],\n                given[\"answer\"],\n                given[\"reason\"],\n                given[\"stated_in\"],\n                out=out,\n                today=day,\n                role=role,\n                message_path=message,\n            )\n        if not sys.stdin.isatty():\n            raise Refused(\n                \"run this yourself in a terminal — the questions are for the maintainer to answer; \"\n                \"an answer stated elsewhere is recorded with --change, --answer, --reason and --stated-in\"\n            )\n        return decide_adr(root, ask=ask, out=out, today=day",

          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, ask: Ask = input, out: Out = print, today: date | None = None) -> int:\n    args = parser().parse_args(argv)\n    root: Path = args.root.resolve()\n    try:\n        if args.verb == \"time-log\":\n            return time_log(root, args, out=out, today=today or date.today())\n        given: dict[str, Any] = {name: getattr(args, name) for name in RECORDING}\n        if any(v is not None for v in given.values()):\n            flags = {name: \"--\" + name.replace(\"_\", \"-\") for name in RECORDING}\n            absent = [flags[n] for n, v in given.items() if v is None or not str(v).strip()]\n            if absent:\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"recording an answer needs all four of {', '.join(flags.values())}; missing or blank: {', '.join(absent)}\"\n                )\n        role = answering_role(root)\n        message = message_path(root)\n        day = today or date.today()\n        if given[\"change\"] is not None:\n            return record_adr(\n                root,\n                given[\"change\"],\n                given[\"answer\"],\n                given[\"reason\"],\n                given[\"stated_in\"],\n                out=out,\n                today=day,\n                role=role,\n                message_path=message,\n            )\n        if not sys.stdin.isatty():\n            raise Refused(\n                \"run this yourself in a terminal — the questions are for the maintainer to answer; \"\n                \"an answer stated elsewhere is recorded with --change, --answer, --reason and --stated-in\"\n            )\n        return decide_adr(root, ask=ask, out=out, today=day",

this change is {klass}.\")\n        endpoint = GLM_FLASH\n    else:\n        if availability_reported is not None or klass is not None:\n            raise Refused(\"--stage2-off explores without a class or a selection receipt.\")\n        # The explicit Stage-1 route skips the class entirely: Haiku explores,\n        # and only the reason is carried for the later plan (spec, criterion 20).\n        endpoint = HAIKU\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, endpoint, bead_file=\"research.md\")\n    key = None\n    route = \"stage-1\" if stage2_off is not None else \"flash\"\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n    extra = (\n        f\"{EXPLORER_ROLE} \"\n        \"Report repository facts with source paths as prose ready to append to `research.md`. \"\n        \"Do not design, recommend, edit a file or use review-table formatting.\"\n    )\n    prompt = work_prompt(root, \"01-explore.md\", change, extra)\n    begin_work_call(ctx, \"explore\", endpoint, prompt, 1, route, ctx.research, stage2_off)\n    answer = run_work_model(ctx, prompt, endpoint, writable=False, key=key)\n    if not names_a_repository_file(root, answer):\n        # Research names its sources; an answer that names no file of the repository is a refusal or a\n        # question, not research, and is shown rather than appended (bead coding-harness-e7m).\n        tail = \"\\n\".join(answer.strip().splitlines()[-40:])\n        print(f\"explore: the answer, as it came:\\n{tail}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        raise CallFailed(\"the exploration answer names no file of the repository; nothing was appended\")\n    # The publication, not a plain append: the header's provenance fields are corrected and the skeleton's\n    # opening notices removed in the same atomic replacement that lands the answer (spec, criteria 1-5).\n    prepared = research_publication(\n        ctx.research.read_bytes(), producer=producer_for(endpoint), day=today(), model=endpoint[1]\n    )\n    publish_research(\n        ctx.research,\n        prepared,\n        f\"## Runner exploration — {today()}\\n\\n{quote_research_records(answer.strip())}\",\n    )\n    print(f\"explore: answer appended to {ctx.research.relative_to(root)} · route {route}\")\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`.           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`).           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number.           "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, ask: Ask = input, out: Out = print, today: date | None = None) -> int:\n    args = parser().parse_args(argv)\n    root: Path = args.root.resolve()\n    try:\n        if args.verb == \"time-log\":\n            return time_log(root, args, out=out, today=today or date.today())\n        given: dict[str, Any] = {name: getattr(args, name) for name in RECORDING}\n        if any(v is not None for v in given.values()):\n            flags = {name: \"--\" + name.replace(\"_\", \"-\") for name in RECORDING}\n            absent = [flags[n] for n, v in given.items() if v is None or not str(v).strip()]\n            if absent:\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"recording an answer needs all four of {', '.join(flags.values())}; missing or blank: {', '.join(absent)}\"\n                )\n        role = answering_role(root)\n        message = message_path(root)\n        day = today or date.today()\n        if given[\"change\"] is not None:\n            return record_adr(\n                root,\n                given[\"change\"],\n                given[\"answer\"],\n                given[\"reason\"],\n                given[\"stated_in\"],\n                out=out,\n                today=day,\n                role=role,\n                message_path=message,\n            )\n        if not sys.stdin.isatty():\n            raise Refused(\n                \"run this yourself in a terminal — the questions are for the maintainer to answer; \"\n                \"an answer stated elsewhere is recorded with --change, --answer, --reason and --stated-in\"\n            )\n        return decide_adr(root, ask=ask, out=out, today=day",

          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable. A leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback. Reviews go by class, and so does phase 1 now (ADR 0020): a `feature` or `architectural` change explores through the research swarm (ADR 0020; a finder trio maps the sources, six seats research eleven topics, online topics on public sources only, Opus 5.5 reconciling; `prepare-explore <change>` first, its report shown to the maintainer, then `explore <change> --availability-reported <id>`; an aborted run resumes; the gate `research-handoff` holds interview and spec to the findings), a `bounded` change or a `spike` through GLM 5.3 Flash; `explore` reads the class from `--class` and the headers of `research.md` and `spec.md`, wherever stated, and refuses missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Artefact lifecycle",
          "end_line": 423,
          "excerpt": "### Artefact lifecycle\n\n```\nplans/specs/<capability>/spec.md          LIVING      — what should hold today\nplans/changes/<name>/                     ACTIVE      — one change in flight\nplans/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/  HISTORICAL  — closed\ndocs/adr/NNNN-title.md                    PERMANENT   — append-only\n```\n\nTwo separate status fields: `status` moves when the project decides;\n`implementation_status` when the code moves. One field for both cannot say\nwhether an accepted spec is still unbuilt or whether built code rests on a\nwithdrawn spec — and those are exactly the interesting cases.\n\nOn close: the delta into the living capability spec, permanent architectural\ndecisions as an ADR, the rest into the archive. **An implemented feature spec\ndoes not stay as a living document** — the code and the git history are the\ntruth. Details in [`plans/_README.md`](../plans/_README.md).\n\nThe **rule against making a second one** stands verbatim in `AGENTS.md`, because\nan agent does not necessarily read `plans/_README.md`: before an artefact is\ncreated, search with `rg` first; where one exists, it is updated. `make\nstaleness` checks the consequences — missing frontmatter, contradictory status,\ndone and never archived, one-sided supersession.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def stamp(path: Path, today: date) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Set `updated:` to today by editing one line. True when the file changed.\n\n    Raises CannotStamp for a file that is not valid UTF-8: reading it with replacement\n    characters and writing it back would change bytes outside the line.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise CannotStamp(f\"not valid UTF-8 ({exc.reason} at byte {exc.start})\") from exc\n    ergebnis = stamped(text, today)\n    if ergebnis == text:\n        return False\n    path.write_bytes(ergebnis.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    return True\n",

          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

Decisions: `decisions.md`.\n\n## Problem\n\nADR 0021 decision 7 currently escalates every consumed review ladder to the maintainer, whereas `AGENTS.md` (PR #419) and the planned runner change `ladder-next-step` (bead `coding-harness-hwll`) direct a consumed ladder to `next: repair <change>` or `next: review <change>`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. `docs/adr/0021-review-swarms-until-clean.md` carries the consumed-ladder amendment stating that a consumed ladder with at least one completed review round names `next: repair <change>` while a taken row is open and `next: review <change>` once every taken row is fixed, including when the loop diff was cut at the line bound.\n   *Refuted by:* ADR 0021 omitting the amendment or failing to state the one-round floor and cut-diff rule.\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`, `decisions.md#Q-2`, `decisions.md#Q-4`, `decisions.md#Q-5`.\n2. When zero review rounds completed in the run, ADR 0021 keeps the escalation stop to the maintainer; the repair brake and every other stop remain unchanged.\n   *Refuted by:* ADR 0021 allowing a zero-round outage to advance to phase 6 or weakening the repair brake.\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-2`, `decisions.md#Q-4`.\n\n## Non-goals\n\nImplementing the runner behavior or rewording `AGENTS.md`; both belong to `ladder-next-step` (bead `coding-harness-hwll`), which merges after this decision pull request.
